title: Best Car and Workshop Vacuum Cleaners UK
short: Wet and dry vacuum cleaners timed sucking up rice, sugar and flour, then five litres of water, to find the best for cleaning cars, garages and workshops.
intro: A car interior needs a proper wet-and-dry vacuum, not a household one, for pulling grit out of footwells and mopping up spilled drinks. This guide is based on Auto Express's tested roundup (26 September 2025), where testers tried every machine in both wet and dry mode: timing how fast each cleared lines of rice, sugar and flour from a carpet mat, then how fast each ingested five litres of water, while also checking hose and cable length, accessories, stability and running costs.

products.name: Multi 20
products.best_for: All-round ability, features and value for most car and garage owners
products.key_spec: 20L capacity, 2.5m hose, wet and dry, blow function, integrated power tool socket
products.summary: Auto Express's overall winner for its all-round ability, features and value, combining strong suction in both wet and dry testing with a useful blow function and a power tool socket for connecting sanders or saws. The 2.5m hose is long enough to reach around most cars without repositioning the unit, and testers rated it a full 5 stars.
pros: Strong suction in both wet and dry modes
Good value for the features included
Blow function and power tool socket
cons: Not the biggest capacity if you need to clean a whole garage in one go

products.name: Multi II 30T
products.best_for: Larger vehicles, garages or workshops needing maximum capacity and suction
products.key_spec: 30L capacity, 4m hose (longest on test), filter-vibration button
products.summary: Auto Express recorded the top suction test scores of the whole group with this larger machine, helped by a filter-vibration button that keeps performance up as the filter clogs. Its 4m hose was the longest on test, reaching right through a car or around a garage without moving the unit, making it the pick for bigger jobs, though it costs more than the Vacmaster.
cons: Bulkier to store than smaller models

guide.q: Why use a wet and dry vacuum instead of a normal one?
guide.a: Auto Express tested every machine here in both dry mode (rice, sugar and flour) and wet mode (five litres of water), something a standard household vacuum isn't built to handle safely. That makes a wet and dry vacuum the right choice for car interiors, where spilled drinks and muddy footwells are common, as well as garages and workshops.

A corded machine like the Vacmaster Multi 20 or Nilfisk Multi II 30T gives unlimited run time and, in testing, the strongest suction. A cordless option like the Stihl SEA 60 is more convenient for quick jobs away from a socket, but Auto Express found it's limited to around 15 minutes on its most powerful setting before needing a recharge.

guide.q: How much does hose length matter?
guide.a: A longer hose lets you reach right through a car or around a garage without moving the unit itself. Auto Express found this varied hugely on test, from 1.4m up to the Nilfisk Multi II 30T's 4m, so it's worth checking if you plan to clean larger vehicles or awkward spaces.

guide.q: What size capacity do I need?
guide.a: For occasional car interior cleaning, a smaller 10-12L tank like the Nilfisk Buddy II 12 is easy to store and enough for the job. For garage or workshop use, or cleaning multiple cars, a larger 20-30L tank like the Vacmaster or Nilfisk Multi II 30T means emptying it less often.
